# Live Pulumi client fixture

`TestPulumiLive` runs the `neon-vercel` client fixture in a protected CI job. The
fixture generates a real Premise Bun TanStack app, a Go environment program,
and separate Go Neon and Vercel components from the tandem registry. It renders
the Vercel component twice and binds two apps in the same environment stack.
`program/main.go` is the client-owned composition. `client-component` demonstrates
a local component with no registry template.

`scaffold.mjs` prepares the test client and its failure-injection tasks. It is test
setup, not an application interface. Clients use normal `pm g`, `pm infra bind`,
`pm infra init/plan/apply`, and optional `pm deploy run` commands. No JavaScript
infrastructure modules or deploy setup script are generated by the templates.

The fixture provisions a branch database and branch-owned GCP Secret Manager
entries first. The application's explicit fnox preview profile reads those values
for migrations and `pm secrets pull`. The full update deploys both apps. The test
checks actual SQL migration history, HTTP reads/writes, remote recovery records,
a failed migration, automatic rollback, failed recovery, and resource cleanup.

Run only with the published RC binary and its matching action:

```sh
PREMISE_LIVE_E2E=1 go test ./e2e -run '^TestPulumiLive$' -timeout 40m -count=1
```

Required inputs are `PREMISE_BIN`, `PREMISE_RC_VERSION`,
`PREMISE_PULUMI_REGISTRY`, and `PREMISE_ACTION_PATH`, plus the dedicated provider
project IDs and CI-only administration credentials documented in the tandem
repository. GCP uses OAuth/workload identity. The identity needs test-project
storage permissions and Secret Manager access to create and remove preview-owned
entries. The backend and shared marker remain after cleanup.

Only `neon-vercel/test-results/workspace/test-results/rollback.json` is a public
artifact. Generated clients, Pulumi state, fnox responses, and environment files
must never be uploaded.
